title: Permission ledger stitching with granular canary consent and audit hierarchy
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Perform a controlled migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 by stitching permission ledgers (primary v1 -> authoritative v2), using an incremental 'ledger-stitch' operator that applies throttled backfills, enables dual-write with audit enrichment, verifies SAML/SSO mappings, and supports customer opt-in canaries. This ticket captures the playbook, automation tasks, observability gates, and comms templates for a low-risk production cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Automated ledger-stitch operator deployed to staging with end-to-end test coverage
Dual-write enabled for 5 pilot orgs; no user-facing permission regressions during 72h
Audit events include v1->v2 translation metadata (old_principal, new_principal, source_tx)
SAML nameID and group attribute mapping validated for pilot orgs and reconciled to <=1% mismatch
Backfill throttling prevents DB CPU > 60% and keeps API tail latency within SLOs
Cutover runbook and customer comms template approved by security and legal
design_notes: We will not rely on a single monolithic backfill; instead use fine-grained ledger shards (by org ID range) to reduce blast radius.
Dual-write will be implemented with idempotent writes and causal metadata (txn_id, source) to allow safe retries.
Audit enrichment adds translation metadata to every permission-change event: {v1_id, v2_id, op, confidence, mapping_rule}

An 'emergency-admin-bypass' feature gate allows ops to grant temporary admin access without modifying primary ledger for incident mitigation; every bypass must emit an audit event tied to a human operator.
SAML mapping verification will use a sampling harness that compares SAML assertion-derived roles to expanded v2 roles and surface mismatches in a dashboard for manual review.
implementation_steps: 1) Build ledger-stitch operator (k8s controller) to read v1 ledger, compute delta, and write to v2 with transactional markers
2) Add dual-write hooks in the auth service with retry queues and dead-letter queues (DLQ) for failed translations
3) Implement backfill throttler: per-org token bucket allowing N writes/sec and global circuit tied to DB metrics
4) Add audit enrichment layer in event pipeline (Kafka topic 'permissions-enriched') with translation metadata
5) Create SAML mapping verifier: automated job that runs daily on pilot orgs to surface mismatches as alerts
6) Deploy to staging and run synthetic canaries that exercise 1k synthetic permissions lookups per minute while running backfill
7) Roll dual-write to pilot cohort (5 orgs), hold for 72h with observability gates
8) Execute phased cutover waves with customer opt-in modal and clear rollback plan
9) Post-cutover 7-day monitoring and a deprecation timeline for v1 read-only mode
observability_gates: API error rate for permission checks < 0.2% (5xx + validation errors)
Audit pipeline lag < 30s for enriched events
Backfill CPU and I/O utilization < 60% of baseline
SAML mapping mismatch rate <= 1% for pilot orgs
rollback_plan: Immediate: flip dual-write flag to v1-only (control plane feature flag)
If control-plane flag fails, run emergency-admin-bypass for affected orgs and route ops to manual fixplaybooks
Backfill: stop operator and reverse marker commits to mark incomplete shards; resume from last known-good checkpoint
Communication: notify pilot orgs via prepared incident template and open dedicated support channel
Telemetry: run diagnostics job that compares v2 effective permissions against snapshot taken pre-cutover to find discrepancies
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: SAML attribute irregularities lead to role mismatches — Mitigation: sampling verifier + customer opt-in canaries + pre-cutover reconciliation run
Risk: Backfill overload causes increased latency — Mitigation: token-bucket throttler + DB circuit breaker + staged shard ordering
Risk: Silent divergence between ledgers — Mitigation: daily reconciliation job and alerting for >0.1% drift in critical roles
Risk: Unauthorized emergency bypass abuse — Mitigation: strict RBAC on bypass feature, mandatory ticket link, and immutable audit event with operator id
open_questions: What minimum pilot cohort size provides statistically meaningful coverage for our largest customers' permission shapes?
Should we expose a self-serve org opt-in in the Console or gate through CSMs for first two waves?
Do we need an offline migration path for air-gapped customers (private deployments)? Currently plan assumes networked control plane.
What SLA do we promise during backfill window for Dedicated customers under contract?
